notes: §1985:VIII.4.4.4 GR5: 'each subsequent OPEN statement execution for that same file must be preceded by the execution of a CLOSE statement, without the LOCK phrase', with status 41 for an open file and 38 for one 'previously closed with lock' (§1985:VIII.1.3.4). FileConnector.OpenOnce returns FileAlreadyOpen (41) on an open connector; FileRegistry.CloseWithLock (reached from RuntimeApi.FileClose's WithLock arm, which the 85 binder admits) adds a successfully closed file to the run unit's lock set and SharedOpenAttempt answers every later OPEN with FileLocked (38) in every mode. The witness reopens a relative file INPUT/I-O/EXTEND/OUTPUT after plain CLOSEs. Probes (b,e): OPEN INPUT on an open file 41 (USE runs, FS=41); CLOSE WITH LOCK then OPEN INPUT/I-O/EXTEND/OUTPUT each 38; READ after the failed OPEN 47, CLOSE after it 42; dynamic-access I-O reopen 00; absent non-optional OPEN I-O 35. (c): OPEN ... SHARING at 85 refused (COBOL2072, its text misleadingly about WHEN OTHER); OPEN EXTEND on a random-access file refused COBOL2372.

next.reason: Reopening in any mode after a CLOSE is kept: §2023:14.9.27.4 GR2 'The file connector referenced by file-name-1 shall not be open' (else status 41), GR4 sets the mode per INPUT/OUTPUT/I-O/EXTEND, and §2023:14.9.6.4 GR8 leaves the connector 'no longer in an open mode'. The 1985 qualifier 'CLOSE statement, without the LOCK phrase' and its status 38 (§1985:VIII.1.3.4) have no 2023 carrier: the 2023 CLOSE format (§2023:14.9.6.2) has no WITH LOCK, so the bar on reopening a file closed with lock is gone.
